subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline controls use shared `MessagePresentation` typed actions with an authenticated `chat.callback` RPC, and where should any capability gate live now that persisted WebChat config is retired?
rationale: The missing feature crosses public Gateway protocol, browser UI behavior, config compatibility, and callback security boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Shared presentation RPC
options.body: Add WebChat inline controls through `MessagePresentation` typed actions plus authenticated `chat.callback`, with explicit session/run binding and no retired `webchat` config.

options.title: Config-gated legacy buttons
options.body: Allow a WebChat capability/config gate and legacy `buttons` payload, accepting conflict with current WebChat config retirement and shared-presentation guidance.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Keep manual text replies for now and route deterministic or webhook actions through existing plugin surfaces until a broader WebChat interaction design is approved.

recommendation.title: Shared presentation RPC
recommendation.body: Add WebChat inline controls through `MessagePresentation` typed actions plus authenticated `chat.callback`, with explicit session/run binding and no retired `webchat` config.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision primarily affects Control UI chat behavior and public product direction, where recent history and issue timeline both point to this owner path.
